item.title: Ozu Castle and Cormorant Fishing — Guide
item.description: Ozu Castle stands above the Hiji River in the castle town of Ozu, sometimes called ‘little Kyoto’ for its old streets and riverside setting. Unusually, its four-storey wooden keep was faithfully reconstructed in the early 2000s using traditional methods and authentic materials, making it one of Japan’s most convincing modern wooden castle rebuilds — you can even stay overnight in the keep as a special experience. In summer, the river below comes alive with ukai, traditional cormorant fishing, in which fishermen in boats use trained cormorants to catch sweetfish by torchlight, a spectacle watched from pleasure boats.
